summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would appropriate money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the Parliamentary Departments to cover the first part of the 2025-26 financial year.

It proposes amounts broadly equal to 5/12ths of the estimated 2025-26 annual appropriations, excluding 2025-26 Budget measures, with the remaining 7/12ths plus Budget measures to come in the Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026.
The bill would commence on the later of 1 July 2025 or Royal Assent, is one of three Supply Bills, and would be repealed at the start of 1 July 2028.
changes: Appropriates the amounts in Schedule 1 for departmental items, administered items, administered assets and liabilities items and other departmental items of the Parliamentary Departments.

Caps the Advance to the responsible Presiding Officer at $300,000 each for the Department of the Senate, the Department of the House of Representatives and the Parliamentary Budget Office, and $1 million for the Department of Parliamentary Services.
Provides that if both this bill and the Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 are enacted, the combined advances cannot exceed $1.9 million.
Declares the Portfolio Budget Statements relevant documents for interpreting the Act and treats notional transactions between non-corporate Commonwealth entities as real payments.
Repeals the Act at the start of 1 July 2028.
summary.affected: The Department of the Senate, the Department of the House of Representatives, the Department of Parliamentary Services, the Parliamentary Budget Office and the Presiding Officers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Moved procedural arrangements to sequence debate and votes on Supply Bills, the Transport Security Amendment Bill 2024, the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment Bill 2025 and the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2025. Said the motion was needed because Senate estimates would prevent later consideration.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Reported that debate time had expired under an earlier resolution and put the questions required to complete consideration of the listed bills; the question was agreed to and the bill was read a second time.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: Moved that Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) be read a second time, seeking $195.3 million from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for parliamentary departments in 2025-26, including over $155 million for the Department of Parliamentary Services.

speeches.speaker: Jenny McAllister
speeches.brief: Tabled proposed and certain proposed expenditure for the year ending on 30 June 2026, including expenditure for parliamentary departments and the Supply Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 and Supply Bill (No. 2) 2025-2026, then moved for referral to legislation committees; the motion was agreed to.
